subject: Post-demo recap & prioritized bakeoff probes for MedAlign
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@medalign.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@medalign.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap & prioritized bakeoff probes for MedAlign

Hi Ethan / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed set of prioritized probes for the bakeoff so your team can validate the three decision criteria you called out. I captured owners and suggested timelines below.

Pain points you emphasized
- Unpredictable inference latency spikes during peak reports (P95 and occasional tail > 2s)
- Large variance in per-token cost when serving long-context workflows (clinical note summarization)
- Data residency and auditability requirements for PHI and retention (you called out 7 years)

Primary goals
- P95 text-generation latency at or under 500ms for 1k-token requests (after batching optimizations)
- Reduce per-token cost by ~30–40% vs current managed endpoint without increasing error rate
- Ensure audit logs and KMS-backed key control for all inference requests in your VPC deployment

Decision criteria (what you'll use to compare vendors)
1) SLO parity: P50/P95/P99 latency at target load, error rates, and quantile stability over 24h
2) Unit economics: effective cost per 1k tokens under your request mix (batching + KV cache savings)
3) Operational controls: VPC, KMS/HSM, retention & auditability, rollout/fallback behaviors

Prioritized bakeoff probes (first sprint - 10 business days)
A. Latency stability probe (owner: Camila) — run 24h steady-state test with your 80:20 short-vs-long request mix; measure P50/P95/P99 and jitter.
B. Cost baseline probe (owner: Irene) — run matched request replay to produce effective cost per 1k tokens for our optimized runtime vs your current endpoint.
C. KV/prefix caching probe (owner: Camila) — evaluate cache hit-rate on repeated context patterns for summarization jobs.
D. Security & audit probe (owner: Marissa) — validate KMS integration, audit log detail, and retention/exports for a 90-day window (we will provide logs stubs).

Open questions we promised to clarify
- Which model family do you want included as the primary candidate for the bakeoff (your team mentioned an in-house Llama-variant and an external MISTRAL variant)?
- Any hard constraints on peak concurrent requests beyond the sample load you sent?
- Procurement contacts and timing for a short term reserved capacity window if we need to guarantee throughput for the tests.

Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-probes.xlsx (probe checklist + metrics to collect), SLA-Draft-v2.pdf (example dedicated SLA we can adapt)

Next steps/action items
- Camila: deliver test harness & dataset + sample load script by Tue 5/18 (ETA)
- Irene: share cost-replay instructions and how to instrument tokens for accurate billing comparison (ETA: 5/18)
- Marissa: share KMS onboarding checklist and first-pass SLA redlines (ETA: 5/19)
- Ethan/Priya: confirm model family preference and final procurement contact by EOD Mon 5/17

If this lines up, we'll schedule an onboarding call for the test run on Wed (5/19) and sync daily for the first 48 hours of the latency probe.

Thanks — looking forward to running the tests.

—
Irene Choi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0128

[Attachment: redwood-bakeoff-probes.xlsx]
[Attachment: SLA-Draft-v2.pdf]

From: Ethan Morris <ethan.morris@medalign.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@medalign.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & prioritized bakeoff probes for MedAlign

Irene / team —

Appreciate the recap, this is exactly the kind of structure we need. Quick answers:
- For model family, prioritize the in-house Llama-variant first (we want to see how external runtimes compare to our tuned weights), but include MISTRAL as a secondary candidate in the same runs.
- Peak concurrency: realistic peak is 120 qps for short requests, 18 concurrent long-context summarizations (1k tokens). We'll share load profiles as a CSV today.
- Procurement: looping in our lead Sourcing contact, Rajesh Patel (rpatel@medalign.com). He can expedite a short reserved capacity purchase if needed.

We'll commit to confirming the model set and procurement contact by EOD today. Please go ahead and provision the test harness. 5/19 onboarding call works for us.

—
Ethan Morris
Head of Platform Engineering | MedAlign Health
ethan.morris@medalign.com | +1 (206) 555-3344

Ethan / Priya —

Thanks — I'll start by standing up the harness using the load CSV once you send it. A couple of technical clarifications so the latency probe is apples-to-apples: 

1) Please confirm whether the 1k-token requests include both prompt + expected continuation (we'll use the same split for measuring end-to-end generation).
2) For the cache probe, can you provide 10 representative prompt families (anonymized) that we can seed into the KV cache? That will let us measure hit-rate improvement realistically.
3) Are there any specific rate-limiter headers or tracing correlation IDs we should mirror from your production clients? Mimicking those will help reproduce tail behavior.

I'll publish an updated probe checklist to the shared Drive and post the link in the HubSpot deal once the harness is live.

Camila
